r: I know of your business at the well the night after the illness broke out.
Can you tell me more about the Shadow?

buceth_10.m: Then, one day, a group of men come walking into the village. Shining armor, white teeth, combed hair, trimmed beards.

buceth_11.m: The men claim that their lord owns this land, including your village.

buceth_12.m: They claim that they keep the land safe of wrongdoers and evil creatures.

buceth_13.m: For their help in protecting your village, they ask that the village compensate them with a share of the harvest.

buceth_14.m: Now, tell me. Would you support those men by agreeing to their terms?

buceth_16.m: Let me continue the story of our hypothetical case.

buceth_17.m: A while later, the men return. They explain that some of the ways things are done in the village have now been prohibited across the whole land.

buceth_18.m: Without going into specifics, let's say that these are ways that have been used for past generations in your village.

buceth_19.m: Changing the way things are done will require quite an effort for people to adjust. A lot of people in the village are upset because of this news from the men.

buceth_2.m: Oh, I am sure you do. But what proof do you have, eh? Anything the guards would believe?

buceth_20.m: Now, tell me. Would you in secret continue using the old ways your past generations have used, or would you instead convert to the ways that the men are advocating?
r: I would continue using the old ways in secret.
I would continue using the old ways, and fight the ruling that prohibited them in the first place.
I would only use the ways that are allowed.
I can't decide without knowing the specifics.

buceth_21_2.m: I am glad to hear that there are people still around that are willing to stand up for what is right.

buceth_22.m: How interesting. You have a different view of the world than what I and the priests of Nor City have.

buceth_23.m: You are of course entitled to your opinion, but you should know that your opinion might conflict with the Shadow.

buceth_24.m: You wanted to know about some business that you accuse me of. Since you have no proof, I will claim innocence. I know that my conscience is clean.
r: Fine. How about I give you some gold instead, would that make you talk?

buceth_25.m: Your views match those that I and the other priests from Nor City believe in. Tell me, would you be interested in following the glow of the Shadow?
r: I am ready to follow the Shadow.
How can I agree to something without knowing what it entails?
No, I will go my own way.
No, I will go my own way. Your stupid Shadow is nothing but talk and fancy words.
(Lie) I am ready to follow the Shadow.

buceth_26.m: If the answers you gave previously were indeed your views, then I can assure you that the path that is guided by the Shadow is the right one.
r: I am ready to follow the Shadow.
No, I will go my own way.
No, I will go my own way. Your stupid Shadow is nothing but talk and fancy words.
(Lie) I am ready to follow the Shadow.

buceth_27.m: I am glad to hear that, but then again, I had a feeling all along that you would say that.

buceth_3.m: Let me ask you something first, and we might talk after that.
r: How about some gold, would that make you talk?

buceth_4.m: Let me start by telling you a story.
r: Let me guess, this story is going to take forever to listen to. How about I give you some gold, and instead we can discuss what you were doing at the well.

buceth_5.m: Let's assume you live in a village that, for the most part, keeps to itself. Your village is self-sustainable and the crops have been good for some years.

buceth_6.m: With the few exceptions of some fights here and there between villagers because of misunderstandings, on the whole, your village is a friendly, peaceful village.

buceth_7.m: You work in the same profession as your parents, which in turn worked in the same professions as their parents.

buceth_8.m: Let's also assume that the way you conduct your business is the same way that the people in the village have been conducting their business for generations past.

buceth_9.m: Everyone respects one another in the village, and your appointed leader does a good job at keeping everyone's interests satisfied, while at the same time being reasonably fair.

buceth_bribed_1.m: You again. Thank you for the gold earlier.

buceth_complete_1.m: Welcome back my friend. May you bask in the glow of the Shadow.

buceth_decline.m: I am sorry to hear that. I guess we do not share views after all.

buceth_dontknow.m: I am sorry to hear that. You should make up your mind and return to me once you have done so. Then we might be able to talk more.
r: How about I give you some gold instead?

buceth_fight_1.m: Infidel, you will not defeat me! For the Shadow!

buceth_follow_1.m: Welcome back my friend. Walk with the Shadow.

buceth_gold_1.m: Hmm, that might be an interesting proposal. How much gold are you suggesting?

buceth_gold_no.m: Hrmpf. Thanks for the gold, but I am not interested in talking to you. Now, please leave.

buceth_gold_yes.m: You seem to realize the true value of the Shadow. Yes, this will do fine, thank you.

buceth_story_1.m: You wanted to ask me something?
r: What were you doing at the well during the night?

buceth_story_10.m: So, currently, that's where we stand now. The deed is done, and the Shadow will look favorably upon us.
r: So, the well was poisoned, that's horrible. How could you?

buceth_story_11.m: Horrible!? What is horrible? What those people from Feygard are doing - that's what's horrible!

buceth_story_12.m: Now, I ask you to keep this story just between us two. You understand that, right?
r: I promise not to tell anyone.
No, I will report you to the guard.

buceth_story_13.m: I urge you to rethink your reasoning. The way of the Shadow is the righteous way.
r: Very well. I promise not to tell anyone.
No. Your crimes will be punished!

buceth_story_15.m: If you want to learn more about the Shadow, please visit the chapel custodian in Nor City. Tell them I sent you, and they will surely extend their gratitude towards you.

buceth_story_2.m: Let me first tell you my background.

buceth_story_3.m: I am appointed by the priests of Nor City to help guide the people of Loneford towards the Shadow. Our mission is to see that the Shadow casts its glow over Loneford as well as other settlements around here.

buceth_story_4.m: Most folk in these northern parts seem too occupied with obeying the will of Feygard and Lord Geomyr. We want to help people see the light of the wrongdoings that Feygard advocates, and to point out the errors in their ways.

buceth_story_5.m: That's my mission here. To see that the Shadow casts its glow over Loneford.
r: How does this relate to what you were doing at the well?

buceth_story_6.m: Nor City sent word to me that something was about to happen here in Loneford. Something that would help our cause.

buceth_story_7.m: They were sending a boy to do some business here, and I was assigned to make sure that the mission was successful.
r: Do you know where he went after he left Loneford?

buceth_story_7_1.m: The boy told me he had some business with a rich man in Brimhaven. Maybe he went there.

buceth_story_8.m: I was tasked with gathering samples from the water in the well and from the ground around the well. Also, I was given some vials whose contents should be poured into the well.

buceth_story_9.m: Apparently, the boy they sent was successful in his mission. The task that I did was also successful, if I may say so myself.

priest_shadow_1.m: The Shadow protects us. It keeps us safe and comforts us when we sleep.

priest_shadow_2.m: It follows us wherever we go. Go with the Shadow my child.

andor.1: My father Mikhail says that Andor has not been home since yesterday. I should go look for him in the village.
andor.10: Leonid tells me that he saw Andor talking to Gruil. I should go ask Gruil if he knows more.
andor.20: Gruil wants me to bring him a poison gland. Then he might talk more. He tells me that some poisonous snakes have such a gland.
andor.30: Gruil tells me that Andor was looking for someone called Umar. I should go ask his friend Gaela in Fallhaven to the east.
andor.40: I talked to Gaela in Fallhaven. He tells me to go see Bucus and ask about the Thieves' Guild.
andor.50: Bucus has allowed me to enter the hatch in the derelict house in Fallhaven. I should go talk to Umar.
andor.51: Umar in the Fallhaven Thieves' Guild recognized me, but must have me confused with Andor. Apparently, Andor has been to see him.
andor.55: Umar told me that Andor went to see a potion maker called Lodar. I should search for his hideaway.
andor.61: I heard a story in Loneford, where it seemed like Andor had been in Loneford, and that he might have had something to do with the illness that the people are suffering from there. I am not sure if it actually was Andor. If it was Andor, why would he have made the people of Loneford ill?
andor.62: Andor might have gone to do some business with a rich man in Brimhaven after he left Loneford.
andor.65: It looks like Andor was involved in the destruction of the Brimhaven dam.
andor.70: I have found the potion-maker Lodar, and heard his story about Andor. Andor went to visit Lodar in his hideaway to get a sample of something called Narwood extract. Lodar happened to notice that there was someone travelling together with Andor, that hid among the trees and did not seem to want Lodar to spot him.
andor.71: Shortly after Andor and the person he was travelling with had left, strange things started to happen in the woods around Lodar's hideaway, and Lodar himself seemed to be affected by it somehow. Lodar believes that something disturbed the tomb below his cabin, and awoke the Hira'zinn.
andor.72: Since I helped Lodar defeat the Hira'zinn, he promised to help me in return. He gave me a piece of paper that should allow me to enter the Valanyr temple of the Shadow in Nor City. He told me to seek out lady Lydalon in the temple for further assistance.
andor.80: All clues so far as to where Andor went point to Nor City. I should travel to Nor City by following the Duleian road to the southeast and look for more clues there.
andor.85: Andor may have been in Stoutford.
andor.86: Andor had something to do with the demon under the church in Stoutford.
andor.90: At Castle Guynmart I learned from Steward Unkorh that some time ago Andor was also there as a guest.
andor.92: Unkorh gave me the bonemeal potion box that Andor had given him for safekeeping.
andor.100: While exploring the town of Sullengard, I so happened to stumble upon my mother and my aunt to whom I have never met. Mother has insisted that I go home so we can talk.
andor.110: After talking with mother back at home, she and I tried to brainstorm about where Andor could be. She reminded me about Andor's friend Stanwick who lives in Brightport. We agreed that going to talk to him might be the next logical thing to do.
andor.120: In the dungeons of Laeroth manor, Kotheses, the torturer, mentioned that he had taught Andor the basics of torturing.
andor.125: Vaelric confirmed that Andor visited him recently. Andor sought to learn Vaelric's skills and left quickly, clutching what he came for. His actions raise more questions about his intentions.
andor.126: In Brightport, I was finally able to meet Stanwick, but due to his hazy memory, he was not able to help me learn anything about the whereabouts of Andor.
andor.127: Regaining his peace of mind after I helped him, Stanwick said he'll tell me more about Andor, once he gathers his thoughts.
andor.128: Stanwick gave me a signet ring that I should show to his father. Jorwick, in Nor City.
andor.130: Andor was trying to find out from Seraphina about terrible monsters in the hideout near the place with the larval burrowers.
andor.131: Elysa in the Brightport's thieves guild told me that Andor has bought a map to the sewers of Feygard.
andor.132: While investigating the Brightport theft I learned from Bryma that Andor was the one who stole the important document, and brought it to her in exchange for her alchemy knowledge.
andor.140: I saw Andor in the mountains of Galmore. We were able to exchange a few words before he disappeared again.
andor.145: I met Andor on the road to Feygard, where he was buying food from Rosmara. He disappeared again.
andor.147: I met Andor on the road to Nor City, where he was buying supplies from Alynndir. He disappeared again.
andor.910: I decided to settle down on the top of Mt. Galmore. For this I needed to find a rich and discreet man to rebuild the ruins according to my wishes. Andor will now have to go and find himself.
andor.912: The construction contract for my new home was completed. I was curious to see what it would look like.
andor.914: I visited my new residence on the top of Mt. Galmore. There I would help the people of Dhayavar as a hero and protect them from villains. Or would I become a villain myself? We'll see.
andor.999: [Quest is not completable at this time.]

loneford.10: I heard a story about Loneford. Apparently, a lot of people have become ill there recently, and some have even died. The cause is still unknown.
loneford.11: I should investigate what could have caused the people of Loneford to become ill. To gather clues, I should ask the citizens of Loneford and the surrounding areas about what they think is the cause.
loneford.21: The guards in the Crossroads guardhouse are certain that the illness in Loneford is caused by some sabotage done by the priests or people from Nor City.
loneford.22: Some villagers in Loneford believe that the illness is caused by the guards from Feygard, in some scheme to make the people suffer even more than they already have.
loneford.23: Talion, the chapel priest in Loneford, thinks that the illness is the work of the Shadow, as punishment for Loneford's lack of devotion to the Shadow.
loneford.24: Taevinn in Loneford is certain that Sienn in the southeast barn has something to do with the illness. Apparently, Sienn keeps a pet around that has approached Taevinn in a threatening manner several times.
loneford.25: I should go see Landa in the Loneford tavern. Rumor has it that he saw something that he doesn't dare tell anyone.
loneford.30: Landa confused me with someone else at first. He apparently saw a boy doing something around the town well during the night before the illness started. He was scared to talk to me at first since he thought I looked like the boy he had seen. Could it have been Andor that he saw?
loneford.31: Also, the night after he saw the boy at the well, he saw Buceth taking samples of the water in the well. Strangely enough, Buceth has not gotten ill like the others in the village.
loneford.35: I should go question Buceth at the Loneford chapel about what he was doing at the well, and about whether he knows anything about Andor.
loneford.41: I have bribed Buceth into talking to me.
loneford.42: I have told Buceth that I am ready to follow the Shadow.
loneford.45: Buceth tells me that he is assigned by the priests in Nor City to make sure the Shadow casts its glow over Loneford. Apparently, the priests had sent a boy to do some business in Loneford, and Buceth was tasked with gathering some samples from the water well.
loneford.50: I have attacked Buceth. I should bring any evidence that Buceth has on him to Kuldan, the guard captain in the longhouse in Loneford.
loneford.54: I have given the vial that Buceth had on him to Kuldan, the guard captain in Loneford.
loneford.55: Kuldan thanked me for solving the mystery of the illness in Loneford. They will start bringing in water with help from Feygard instead of drinking from the well from now on. Kuldan also told me to visit the castle steward in Feygard if I want to help further.
loneford.60: I have promised to keep Buceth's story a secret. If Andor was indeed here, he must have had a good reason for doing what he did. Buceth also told me to visit the chapel custodian in Nor City if I want to learn more about the Shadow.

sk.fightstyleUnarmedUnarmored: Fighting style: Way of the monk
